item.title: Starting October 1, WhatsApp to 'stop' delivering messages from these users
item.description: WhatsApp Business users must add payment methods by September 30 to avoid delivery issues with service messages starting October 1. Currently free, these messages will incur charges based on market rates. This change is a part of Meta's ongoing pricing updates and emphasizes the necessity for businesses to prepare their accounts adequately to prevent any service disruptions.

item.title: Scotch whisky gets cheaper in India after trade deal with US; check new prices
item.description: Under the India-UK agreement, the import tariff on British whisky was reduced to 75% from 150%, effectively cutting the rate by half. The tariff is scheduled to decline further to 40% over the next 10 years. However, the reduction in import duty does not result in a similar reduction in the final retail price.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Neerja in 1986, Machchhar in 2026: 2 heroes who put passengers before themselves
item.description: Neerja Bhanot, a flight attendant, showed immense courage during the 1986 hijacking of Pan Am Flight 73 in Karachi. She helped many passengers escape despite the danger, ultimately sacrificing her life. In 2026, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot during a flight and successfully regained control of the aircraft. His actions prevented a mid-air disaster, saving 174 lives onboard.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: Drive wrong, pay more: Karnataka mulls Rs 5,000 fine for repeat traffic offenders
item.description: The Karnataka government is considering increasing fines for traffic violations, particularly for habitual offenders. This proposal includes escalating penalties and accumulating negative points for repeat violations. Additionally, the government plans to ban half-helmets to enhance safety for two-wheeler riders. Measures for regulating low-speed electric two-wheelers and promoting carpooling are also under discussion. Efforts are being made to improve public transport facilities and enforce traffic rules more strictly.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: South Carolina family permanently protects 2,000-acre farm from development
item.description: A family in South Carolina has successfully established a conservation easement to safeguard 2,000 acres of Creekland Farms from future development. Nestled in the rapidly expanding Laurens County, this agreement not only preserves the land's agricultural and recreational uses but also links it to the neighboring Sumter National Forest. It illustrates a proactive strategy in managing urban growth while cherishing rural landscapes.

item.title: In 2018, Musk gave $480,350 for Flint school filters; students drink from fountains
item.description: In a progressive move, Flint Community Schools have transitioned from bottled water to innovative water filtration systems, a project backed by Elon Musk in 2018. Thoroughly tested and redesigned, these 130 stations now furnish clean water by eliminating harmful lead and bacteria. While the water quality is confirmed safe, the school will maintain the provision of bottled water as a precautionary measure.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Texas turns 160 donated Christmas trees into underwater fish reef
item.description: The year 2024 marked an innovative project at Granger Lake, where more than 160 Christmas trees were creatively transformed into a fish habitat. This initiative, a partnership between Yeti, the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, is designed to support smaller fish by providing cover, encouraging the presence of larger sport fish like crappie.

item.title: Piyush Goyal gets a ‘trade minister for life’ tag from US trade chief at G20
item.description: At the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee, US trade representative Jamieson Greer discussed key trade issues with Indian minister Piyush Goyal. They focused on food security, steel overcapacity, and the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, which Greer suggested re-examining. Goyal emphasized the importance of distinguishing between legitimate measures and the weaponization of food supply chains. Discussions also included efforts toward finalizing an interim India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement, enhancing cooperation in manufacturing.

item.title: Senior citizen wrongly paid tax on Rs 25.42L interest; ITAT orders Rs 9.91L refund
item.description: Each year, the senior citizen reported the interest earned from his investments in tax-free bonds under the ‘exempt income’ category in his income tax return (ITR). But made a mistake in one year. The man realised the error only after the deadline for filing a revised ITR had passed. He therefore approached the jurisdictional assessing officer (JAO) and filed a rectification application.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Asian Games: Manu, Prince win sailing silver as India’s medal tally reaches 62
item.description: Manu Francis and Prince Noble secured a silver medal in men’s skiff sailing at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Their final race concluded with a second-place finish, accumulating a total of 23 net points. The Indian duo's consistent performance included three second-place finishes and one race victory across the event. India’s overall medal tally for the Games rose to 62, showcasing their achievements in various sports.

item.title: Man in WagonR with ‘POLICE’ sticker caught stealing plant from Delhi-Dehradun E-way
item.description: A CCTV video capturing a plant theft from a police-marked vehicle has become widely shared on social media. The incident occurred on the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, although no complaints have been reported yet. Police are in the process of verifying the authenticity of the viral footage for further investigation. This incident follows a previous theft involving nearly 7,000 potted plants after a horticulture event.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: ‘You’re giving a go by to rules, acts ... doing your own thing’: Bombay HC to EC
item.description: The Bombay high court expressed concern over the Election Commission's SIR process after several names were removed. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar questioned the legality of the actions taken during the SIR. They highlighted the suspension of several laws under the Representation of People Act and related rules. A family from Santa Cruz brought the matter to the court's attention following their removal from the electoral rolls.
item.dc:creator: LISA MONTEIRO

item.title: 5 money changes in Oct: Bulk FD rates, UPI MDR, SBI ATM limit cut, LPG KYC & more
item.description: The money changes include a reduction in the number of free ATM transactions for certain State Bank of India (SBI) salary account customers, new disclosure norms for interest rates on bulk fixed deposits (FDs), revised charges under the National Pension System (NPS) and mandatory Aadhaar authentication for receiving LPG subsidies.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Asian Games: India win women’s team squash bronze after Anahat Singh’s heartbreak
item.description: India's women's squash team claimed a bronze medal after facing a 1-2 defeat from Hong Kong in the semifinals. Anahat Singh's match was intense, yet she fell short despite holding match points. Tanvi Khanna fought back to equalise, but ultimately, Joshna Chinappa couldn't secure victory against Ho Tze Lok in the decisive match. This result contributes to India's notable achievement of four squash medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: LPG price hike: 19-kg commercial cylinder gets Rs 62.50 costlier
item.description: The cost of 19-kg commercial LPG cylinders has surged by Rs 62.50, now totaling Rs 2,810. Similarly, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices have jumped by around Rs 16 per litre, reaching Rs 137. From October 1, 2026, users will need biometric Aadhaar authentication to book subsidized LPG refills. Failure to register will still allow access to LPG at market rates without any subsidies.

item.title: Kynan Chenai's golden charm: How father's 30-yr-old gun helped him win Asiad gold
item.description: Kynan Chenai won Asian Games mixed team trap gold with Neeru Dhanda using a 30-year-old gun borrowed from his father Darius Chenai, a two-time national trap champion who won both his titles with the same barrel. Kynan calls his father one of his biggest inspirations and the biggest support in his shooting career. From Rio 2016 to his Los Angeles 2028 goal, Kynan says he is “more hungry” now.

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million Six Flags investment faces potential sale
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $200 million Six Flags investment faces a fresh setback as Jana Partners urges the theme park operator to explore a potential sale. The company reported a $203 million second-quarter loss, while attendance fell 7% year over year. Six Flags shares have also dropped sharply from their annual high. The operator is also facing lawsuits involving its X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Wife locked in bedroom and a missing caretaker: Ex-IAS officer’s murder gets murkier
item.description: Nishi Agrawal found her husband Rakesh murdered in their home, with the caretaker Varun now a prime suspect. She discovered her bedroom door was locked from the outside, prompting immediate action from the cook Amar. They found evidence of a potential gas leak, indicating a possible motive for arson. Police believe the murder occurred between 12:30 am and 2:00 am while Varun was seen on CCTV escaping around 2:15 am.

item.title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gambhir questions pitch after India chase 406 with ease
item.description: Gautam Gambhir, India's cricket coach, expressed his worries about the alarming trend of high scores in recent games. He highlighted the pressing need for improved pitch conditions that favour bowlers just as much as batsmen. In a thrilling match, India successfully chased 405 runs, demonstrating outstanding batting skills. Gambhir stressed the importance of fostering pressure-filled situations for young bowlers to aid in their growth.

item.title: Will take China help if Centre and Manipur fail to act: Naga group
item.description: Tangkhul Naga leaders expressed concern over the safety of civilians living in vulnerable border areas. They criticized both the Manipur state government and the central government for their inaction. Recent violence has led to the deaths of multiple Naga civilians, raising significant fears among the affected communities. The group urged for immediate protective measures to prevent seeking assistance from neighboring countries.

item.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp, promises truth 'in due time', wishes team-mates luck
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal’s camp ahead of Thursday’s Nations League clash with Denmark following a dispute over his role under new head coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo confirmed his departure after Jesus said he would not start the match. The 41-year-old has not announced his international retirement, but said he would reveal the reasons for his decision “in due time.”

item.title: 'Receiving necessary medical attention': Embassy updates on Indian Flydubai pilot
item.description: A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv experienced a serious incident that required an emergency landing. Following a cockpit altercation, one pilot was arrested and investigated by Saudi authorities. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the situation was managed and the safety of passengers was prioritized. Warplanes were scrambled in response to potential hijacking fears but were later stood down.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Bombs without brakes? US-China AI race may be harder to control than the nuclear one
item.description: The people building artificial intelligence keep reaching for the same comparison. Billionaire Elon Musk has called AI “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic boss Dario Amodei describes the most powerful models as “weaponisable nuclear materials.” Sam Altman, when asked how AI could be policed, often points to the International Atomic Energy Agency(IAEA), the world's nuclear watchdog.

item.title: Trump announces $200bn South Korean investment in US, $54bn for Alaska LNG
item.description: South Korea is making waves with a monumental commitment of $200 billion toward US energy endeavors. This ambitious plan encompasses a critical liquefied natural gas project in Alaska and a gas-fired power facility in Texas. Moreover, investments in eight nuclear reactors across the nation are also underway. These strategic ventures stem from a $350 billion trade agreement signed in November 2025, reinforcing economic cooperation between South Korea and the US.
